description:
FOUND + FIXED s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10), probed vs perl 5.40.3.

THE BUG.  `p-system`'s multi-argument branch called
`sb-ext:run-program CMD ARGS :search t`, which SIGNALS a simple-error when
:search finds no such program.  Nothing caught it, so the whole top-level form
died: `system { "lskdfj" } "lskdfj"` at t/op/exec.t:109 took every row after it
with it (16 rows never produced).

PERL (probed, all three forms):
    system { "x" } "x"      rc=-1  $?=-1  $!=ENOENT
    system("x", "a")        rc=-1  $?=-1  $!=ENOENT
    system("x")             rc=-1  $?=-1  $!=ENOENT
PCL now matches the first two.

THE FIX.  One `handler-case` around the spawn, returning -1 and setting
`$?` to -1 and `$!` from errno -- which is EXACTLY the handler `p-exec` has
carried all along (rule 11: the mechanism existed, one call site did not use
it).  The spawn itself moved into `%p-system-run` so the handler wraps one
form and the function stays short.

NOT TAKEN, and why: the ONE-ARGUMENT form still goes through /bin/sh
unconditionally, so `system "lskdfj-nope"` is 32512 (the shell's 127<<8) and
$! is 0 where perl gives -1/ENOENT.  perl execs the words DIRECTLY when the
string carries no shell metacharacter (doio.c's metachar scan), and `p-exec`
already has that predicate inline.  Routing p-system through it would change
how EVERY one-string `system` in the suite runs, so it is a separate,
measured change -- filed as a note here rather than done blind.

RESULT: t/op/exec.t 24/1 -> 37/4 (with #1921), 14 FIXED ROWS, 0 NEW, its
16-row shortfall -> 0.  Bars: corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111; the full
perl-tests sweep GATE clean, TOTAL 18686 (+0), drops 5 = census.
subject: FIXED s473t6c: `system` must NEVER die when the child cannot be started -- perl returns -1, sets $? to -1 and $! from the failed exec
